newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble edges up on position-closing, T-bill buying.
newsitem.headline: Rouble edges up on position-closing, T-bill buying.

text.p: Russian banks which had expected rouble depreciation cut long dollar positions, pushing the rouble up in calm trade on Wednesday after the central bank maintained Tuesday's rates, dealers said.
Some banks readying to invest in Treasury bills, on expectations that Western demand would drop at Wednesday's auction, placed additional pressure on the dollar, they said.
"Late yesterday dollar rates were one to two points higher than the central bank's rates. Banks must have bought too many dollars yesterday (anticipating further dollar rise)," one dealer said.
"Today they have to cut their long dollar positions as the central bank kept its rates unchanged," he added.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,436-39 per dollar throughout the day. Late on Tuesday they traded lower at 5,441-42 per dollar. Tomorrow roubles edged up to 5,437-40 per dollar from 5,439-41 late on Tuesday.
The central bank did not change its rate, 5,429/5,439 bid and offer, from Tuesday.
Overnight rouble credit rates rose to 10-20 percent compared with Tuesday's late 0.5-5.0 percent, which dealers said indicated increased domestic interest in T-bills.
United Investment Bank chief dealer Alexander Suchkov said rouble demand could be higher today as banks were awaiting a price fall on the government bond market.
"Overnight rates have risen today the first time since T-bill yields have started to fall. After that many Russian banks and investors decreased their T-bill investments," Suchkov said.
Foreigners, who have recently pumped new funds into the bond market, on Wednesday faced new rules which decreased guaranteed foreign yields to 16 percent from 19 percent annually.
